fields.struck_reason: Retired 2026-10-03. This was the farm quilt: 119 Voronoi crop cells over 3.84 km2, with hedgerow trees along its 310 internal edges and dark blobs on its margins. docs/design/WHAT-THE-WORLD-IS.md 2.1 names it the wrong land use, and R0045 forbids a large tree in open meadow, which a 4 km hedge wall through a meadow plainly is. Cultivation continues as each homestead's own plot (land_use.homesteads[].plot); the ground is no longer partitioned. The partition code and its independent-oracle tests are kept, not deleted: the plots are polygons too, and a plot that follows a hedgerow is not the design.

An airborne wind turbine on a 330 m tether at 64 deg, tied under the hull's head, so the hull's centre rides ~370 m above the ground and its keel ~250 m above the tallest redwoods, downwind of its mast.

kinds.where: the scarp and the north plateau, the meadow-edge band at the forest boundary, the river corridor, and a homestead's or the village's own screen. Never in open meadow: R0045, and landuse.tree_allowed_at is the predicate that decides it
kinds.authority: shared/terrain/forest.py derives the spacing from this closure and the species' measured crown width, then measures the instance count. landuse.tree_allowed_at owns WHERE a tree may stand; it is not re-implemented. 2026-10-04: the human chose 0.80. There is deliberately no spacing_m and no count here. Both are outputs of the rule, and a concluded number written into this file is the same category error as a guessed one: it drifts the moment the crown asset is rebuilt, and it drifts silently, because nothing recomputes it.

camera.note: The climb at the end is deliberate: the northern peaks enter frame as the camera rises, and the last beat is the widest.
camera.yaw_convention: degrees counter-clockwise from +X (east) toward +Y (north), seen from above with +Z up; 0 is east, 90 is north, positive turns north. Pitch is degrees below horizontal, negative is looking down.
camera.fov_note: 28 mm on a 36 mm sensor. The map did not declare a lens; the preview used 28 mm and the composition read, so it is recorded here rather than left to each client.

clearance.rule: The path must not pass through any placed object, and no unrendered area may be visible.
clearance.edge_disclosure: At 250 m the true horizon is roughly 50 km, so a 4088 m block cannot fill frame by itself. The block edge must be dissolved by aerial perspective before the path reaches its end. This makes the brief's aerial-perspective requirement load-bearing rather than decorative: without it the world visibly ends.

wind.label: W
wind.note: Down the valley, from the west: the bearing is where the wind comes from, so it blows toward 95, the way the river runs from the western gorge (-2048, -100) to the low eastern gap (2048, -420). A deep valley channels the air along its axis. The regional flow over the ring of ridges is the westerly that loads the snow (a compressed Sierra, storms from the west-south-west), and the walls turn it down the valley; the cross-valley part is blocked. The thermal winds are real but diurnal: the up-valley breeze from the east blows only on sunny afternoons and reverses at night, and the down-slope drainage off the northern massif is a shallow night flow, not a wind for generators riding hundreds of metres up. One prevailing wind serves every consumer, and the ones that record climate need it: the snow drifts and the Granite Cirque lie on the lee, east-facing side, and cumulus at 1,000-1,600 m drifts with the westerlies aloft.
shared_by: turbines and generator blimps (face it, trail downwind)

heightmap.note: row r is y = 2044 - 8r, so the image is stored south-up: an image viewer shows north at the bottom.

field_albedo.note: Same orientation and origin as the heightmap. RGB is the crop swatch written unchanged; it is not sRGB-corrected or colour-managed here.

water_mask.note: Same orientation and origin as the heightmap.

far_field.covers: The ground the block does not reach: the ring of ridges that closes the valley, the river's two valley reaches and the northern skyline past the block's own edge at y = 2044.
far_field.seam: Vertex for vertex with the block. 56 m divides the 4088 m grid, so a far-field vertex sits exactly on each block edge, and every far-field vertex inside the block carries the block's own height: inside it is the block, beyond it is the same generator run coarse.
far_field.note: Same orientation, encoding range and row order as the heightmap: row r is y = 12036 - 32r. The encoding range is not repeated here: it is block.height_range_m, and both rasters are written against it, so one decode serves either and there is no second number to keep in step.

valley_outline.note: The valley's outline, so no edge of it runs along a coordinate axis. front_bend moves the northern mountain front north (+) or south (-) of the straight start lines, by easting: spurs under the massifs, bays between them. trail_lock holds the front where it stands north of y_m[1] between x_m, because the graded trails and the turbines stand there; south of it the front still bends. rim_radius_m is where the walls begin elsewhere, one radius per 15 degrees of bearing counter-clockwise from east around rim_centre_xy_m, kept 240 m or more from every homestead. The wander terms are low-frequency noise on both.

bowls.label: Granite Cirque
bowls.note: The hollow the glaciers left, found by sites.py. Its shape is the land's own; this only names it.

enclosure.note: The valley is a temporary flat-ish land hidden between mountains. Past mountains.valley_outline's rim the ground rises into a ring of crags over width_m, buttressed along the fall line; the rim runs inside the block's corners and south edge, so the walls are real 8 m terrain there. The river arrives down a gorge from higher ground in the west and leaves through a broad low gap in the east. Each reach's polyline is [x, y, water surface z] in metres, starting where the block's own river polyline ends, and is read by the core to shape the ground and by clients to draw the water. North of the block the ring stays at the generator's own ground inside north_basin, the hollow the old city towers stood in; it is kept so the northern skyline did not move when they went.

horizon.note: Display only, written by shared/terrain/horizon.py past the far field's edge: high country the valley is cut into. Each reach continues a river reach: upstream it climbs into a notch, downstream the valley bends so the gap closes on itself. Heights here may exceed block.height_range_m; they are not in either height raster.

massif.note: The mountains, grown by shared/terrain/massif.mjs from this history. Heights live in shared/world/out/massif.f32.

upstream_river.note: The river above the block follows the drainage of the grown land; massif.mjs traces it and shared/terrain/river_course.py publishes it to river_reaches.

land_use.authority: docs/design/LAND-USE-R0051.md sections 1-4. Counts are outputs of the measured bench and the declared catchment, not parameters.

bench.measured: recomputed from the heightfield and worldmap.water.bodies on every run; not a stored constant

tree_rule.rule: R0045: no large tree in open meadow. Allowed on the forest slope, in the band at the meadow's edge, in the river corridor, and within a homestead's or the village's own screen. Forbidden in open meadow. The village screen is not decoration: Big Sur's rule is that existing topography OR TREES screen the buildings, so a village sited to be screened has to be a place this rule permits trees in.
